newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, NATO say way open to sign deal on May 27.
newsitem.headline: Russia, NATO say way open to sign deal on May 27.

text.p: NATO Secretary General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov said agreement at talks on Wednesday opened the way for Moscow and the Western alliance to sign a security deal on May 27.

"Reason has prevailed. The road to signing on May 27 is clearly open," Solana told reporters after he and Primakov agreed the terms of a new relationship between NATO and Moscow. The agreement must be approved by President Boris Yeltsin and NATO heads of government before it is signed.
Primakov also said the door was open to signing the agreement in Paris on the date set by Yeltsin.

"If approved, the path to signing the document in Paris will be clear," he told reporters. "It is a big victory for reason, it is a big victory for the world community and it is a big victory for Russia and all governments in the world interested in peace and cooperation."

Agreement was reached on the deal, intended to address Russian concerns about NATO's eastward expansion, after months of negotiations headed by Primakov and Solana. Each praised the other for defending their respective interests.

"I do think we can be very proud about what we have achieved at this point in the agreement and without any doubt we will open a new age in the history of NATO relations with Russia and the stability of our countries," Solana said.
